reasons: The data is organised clearly and helpers are simple.
Some companies appear twice under different IDs.
Domain lookup can return vendor domains.

terms.meaning: applicant tracking system, the hiring software a company uses for job applications
the account name a company uses on a hiring platform
the main web address of an organisation, such as example.com
browser storage that keeps data across page refreshes

sections.name: File setup, Region, Sector, ATSPlatform
sections.title: Region, sector and hiring system labels
sections.what: Defines the allowed values for region, sector and hiring system, which are used to label every company.
sections.why: These labels let the app filter companies.
sections.watch_out: A new region or sector must be added here before companies can use it.

sections.name: CompanyTarget
sections.title: Company record shape
sections.what: The shape of one company entry: name, regions, sector, hiring system, optional tenant name, careers link, and an on or off switch.
sections.why: Gives every company the same fields.
sections.watch_out: The tenant name is filled only for some companies, so do not assume it exists.

sections.name: CONSULTING_GLOBAL
sections.title: Top global consulting firms
sections.what: Fourteen leading consulting firms with a global reach, presented as the first tier.
sections.why: The comment labels these as the top tier, so they are grouped first.
sections.watch_out: Several entries use general careers pages, so their links may need updating.

sections.name: CONSULTING_ME
sections.title: Middle East consulting firms
sections.what: Five consulting firms with a Middle East focus.
sections.watch_out: Redseer appears here and again in the India list under a different ID, so it can show twice.

sections.name: CONSULTING_APAC
sections.title: Asia Pacific consulting firms
sections.what: Three consulting firms for Asia Pacific, one of which is switched off.
sections.watch_out: The switched-off entry will not appear in any search.

sections.name: CONSULTING_INDIA
sections.title: India consulting firms
sections.what: Five consulting firms focused on India.
sections.watch_out: Frost and Sullivan's careers link is the same as the Asia Pacific entry, so two entries share one link.

sections.name: BIG_TECH
sections.title: Large technology companies
sections.what: Twelve large technology companies with strategy, operations or business roles.
sections.why: Keeps large tech targets separate from consulting.
sections.watch_out: Several entries use custom hiring systems, so automated checks may not work for them.

sections.name: AI_EMERGING
sections.title: AI and emerging technology companies
sections.what: Sixteen AI and frontier technology companies, mostly with a global reach.
sections.why: Groups AI companies into their own category.
sections.watch_out: These use the sector name ai-emerging, while buckets.ts uses a different name, so they are not linked automatically.

sections.name: ME_REGIONAL
sections.title: Middle East technology and investment companies
sections.what: Twenty-one employers across technology, investment and industry, mostly in the UAE and Saudi Arabia.
sections.why: The comment describes this as the regional focus.
sections.watch_out: NEOM and The Line share one careers link.

sections.name: APAC_REGIONAL
sections.title: Asia Pacific technology companies
sections.what: Sixteen technology and e-commerce employers across Asia Pacific.
sections.watch_out: Entries with a custom hiring system may need manual checks.

sections.name: INDIA_REGIONAL
sections.title: India technology companies
sections.what: Twenty technology, fintech and AI employers in India.
sections.watch_out: Reliance Jio and Jio Platforms share one careers link.

sections.name: DEFAULT_COMPANY_TARGETS
sections.title: Default company list
sections.what: Joins all the regional lists into one default list, and declares the storage key used to save user changes.
sections.why: Gives a single starting point when nothing is saved.
sections.watch_out: A new list must be added here or it will never show by default.

sections.name: getCompanyTargets
sections.title: Reading the company list
sections.what: Returns the list the user saved in browser storage, or the defaults if nothing is saved or the saved data is broken.
sections.why: Lets users keep their own changes.
sections.watch_out: Once a user saves a list, later updates to the defaults do not reach that user.

sections.name: saveCompanyTargets
sections.title: Saving the company list
sections.what: Writes the full company list to browser storage.
sections.why: Stores user edits such as switching companies on or off.
sections.watch_out: It does not notify the rest of the page, unlike some sibling stores.

sections.name: resetCompanyTargets
sections.title: Resetting the company list
sections.what: Replaces the saved list with the built-in defaults.
sections.why: Lets the user undo their edits.
sections.watch_out: It erases all user edits to the list without any confirmation in this code.

sections.name: getEnabledTargets
sections.title: Filtering enabled companies
sections.what: Returns only switched-on companies, optionally limited to one region or sector.
sections.why: Lets searches run only for companies the user wants.
sections.watch_out: A company listed under several regions appears once for each region that matches the filter.

sections.name: companyDomain
sections.title: Email domain from careers link
sections.what: Turns a company's careers web address into its main domain, which is needed for email lookup.
sections.why: Email lookup needs the company domain, not a careers page address.
sections.watch_out: Some careers links point to a hiring vendor, so the domain returned belongs to the vendor, not the company.

summary: Holds the built-in list of about 110 target companies, grouped by type and region, with their careers links and hiring systems, plus helpers to read, save, reset, filter and derive email domains.
purpose: Gives the app a ready list of employers to search and to watch for openings.
why: The header says users can turn companies on or off, or add their own, through the config page. The grouping by region and sector lets the app filter the list.
how: 1. Defines the labels for region, sector and hiring system. 2. Defines the company records in regional lists. 3. Combines them into a default list. 4. Reads the saved list from browser storage, falling back to the defaults. 5. Filters by enabled status, region and sector. 6. Turns a careers link into a domain for email lookup.
inputs: Nothing for the fixed lists. Helpers take optional region and sector filters, and a company record for domain lookup.
outputs: Company lists, filtered company lists, and a domain name or null.
risks: A saved list overrides later changes to the defaults, so users may not see new companies. Several entries share the same careers link or duplicate a company. Domain lookup can return a hiring vendor's domain instead of the company's.
debug: If a company is missing, check whether it is enabled and whether the saved list in browser storage replaced the defaults. Use the reset function to restore the built-in list.
